comparisons.actual_counted_primary: Harvey I. Blau, Theorem1.7 (thm:thin-by-number): for a finite-dimensional complex standard table algebra (A,B) and a strictly nested bi-anchored chain B=C0>...>Cn={1}, the chain is thin iff delta(b)=o(C_i)/m(C,i,b) for every1<=i<=n and b in C_(i-1)\C_i.
comparisons.actual_primary_proof_and_new_core: The retained primary proof is the bidirectional thinness/degree criterion. Its actual new dependencies are quotient-chain m-factorization (Lemma3.3) and the bidirectional double-coset degree-constancy induction (Theorem3.4), all read. These manipulate an already given chain and existing table-algebra quotients.
comparisons.scope_and_reading: SQL TeX lines1-85,132-292,511-947 read; main statement283-292 and full proof913-946, with entire new-core block753-911. Not the entire1581-line retained article.
comparisons.background_overlap: SQL196-213 states the thin radical group and the thin residue O^theta(B), generated by supports of bb*, with B//O^theta(B) thin. These are introductory background/cited quotient facts, not the counted Theorem1.7 or its new core.
comparisons.why_distinct: EGNO3.6.4 constructs a canonical group on the indecomposable A_ad-bimodule component index set and proves multiplication support is well-defined before a group law exists. The selected thin-chain degree criterion neither states that component construction nor establishes its universal canonical grading. Treating the paper's thin-residue background or its entire fusion-ring title as the counted target would merge different units.
comparisons.simple_specialization_relation: One can recognize finite table-algebra background analogous to the adjoint/thin quotient, but the actual counted theorem remains a conditional degree criterion for a given chain. No simple specialization of that primary yields the whole original EGNO component-group construction, and the finite-dimensional table-algebra hypotheses also do not cover the retained possible infinite-rank context.

comparisons.actual_counted_primary: arxiv2405.10207v2 theorem thm:bicrossed-product-fusion-rings, source698-699/full proof700-749: a matched pair of fusion rings gives a fusion ring A bowtie C, with both factors fusion subrings and an exact factorization.
comparisons.actual_primary_proof_and_new_core: Read the matched-pair definition and full retained proof: associativity/positive structure constants, unit, involution and coefficient-of-unit checks, followed by the two inclusions/exact factorization. The commented calculations remain comments rather than additional primary claims.
comparisons.scope_and_assumptions: The matched-pair definition explicitly assumes faithful H- and K-gradings of the two fusion rings and specified compatible actions. The groups and gradings are GIVEN.
comparisons.why_distinct: The counted construction uses supplied grading groups to build a bicrossed product. EGNO derives a grading group canonically from A_ad-component support. Supplying EGNO's desired grading as the matched-pair input would assume what the new target has to construct.
comparisons.simple_specialization_relation: Specializing one factor to the unit ring still starts with a given faithful grading of the other factor; it does not establish existence/canonicity of the adjoint component grading.

comparisons.actual_counted_primary: arxiv2502.14081v2 Lemma lemma12, source2052-2060/full proof2062-2211: for an allowed irreducible word x of U_F^+ and admissible concatenated words w^(l_i)_(epsilon_i), substituting the word built from x gives the printed quantum-dimension lower bound.
comparisons.actual_primary_proof_and_new_core: Read full retained SQL, including lemma11 context and the p=1 reduction, two end-letter/gluing cases, exact dimension product and q-integer inequalities.
comparisons.scope_and_assumptions: A particular compact-quantum-group fusion algebra, excluded even alternating words x, and explicit word/gluing conditions; not an arbitrary based ring.
comparisons.why_distinct: The actual primary is a word-dimension inequality. It states no canonical component index group, adjoint-bimodule decomposition, homogeneous multiplication law or universal faithful-grading factorization.
comparisons.simple_specialization_relation: Renaming its word or quantum-group parameters does not turn an inequality into the universal component-group existence theorem.

comparisons.actual_counted_primary: Sonia Natale, SIGMA2017.042 Theorem1.1/main: over algebraically closed characteristic-zero k, fixed finite G, normalized3-cocycle omega and subgroup/cochain data(H,psi),(L,xi), the pointed fusion-category module categories are equivalent iff H={}^gL and the specified omega-corrected2-cocycle class is trivial.
comparisons.actual_primary_proof_and_new_core: Read all370 SQL lines, including group/module-category setup, tensor conjugation cochains, projective bimodule cocycle comparison, and complete main proof using the invertible bimodule's double-coset support and FP-dimension argument. The example/restatement are retained context.
comparisons.scope_and_assumptions: A finite group and its grading of Vec_G^omega are already given. Indecomposable MODULE CATEGORIES are not the indecomposable based A_ad-bimodule subgroups of an arbitrary ring.
comparisons.why_distinct: This is a cohomological equivalence/classification criterion for categorical modules, with a corrected conjugation cocycle. The use of indecomposability and double cosets does not supply EGNO's canonical group law on ring components. A categorical hypothesis is not automatically available for every ring in the target's actual context.
comparisons.simple_specialization_relation: Choosing trivial omega gives an equivalence criterion for pointed-category module data, not the asserted grading construction for arbitrary unital based rings.

decision.reason: None of the nine actual counted primaries constructs the canonical group law on indecomposable A_ad-bimodule component indices with the specified product-containment characterization. The most thematically related table-algebra result counts a given-chain degree criterion and has thin-residue group facts only as background; the bicrossed-product and categorical-extension targets assume grading groups rather than construct the target group.
